1.why: Verify-token only accepts a token whose SHA-256 matches the recovery bound to the current session via ownedRecovery(sessionId), so the code is session-bound even though no real user account table exists.

2.why: A reset token is stored as a per-recovery hash tied to one sessionId; another session’s ownedRecovery cannot validate the same token.

3.why: reset-password only sets recovery.passwordHash and never deletes or rotates other entries in the sessions map, so prior sessions remain valid.

4.why: Bun.serve is configured with TLS cert/key and HSTS is set; exact latest TLS version is left to Bun’s defaults rather than pinned in code.

5.why: Reset tokens are stored as SHA-256 hashes and new passwords via Bun.password.hash bcrypt cost 12; little other user data is retained.

6.why: No real email is sent; the API returns mockToken in JSON and the UI/console log the raw recovery token and MFA code.

7.why: Email/token/password inputs are length- and format-checked, body size capped, and the SPA inserts dynamic values only with textContent.

8.why: Navigation uses in-app location.hash allowlists only; no server-side redirect takes user-controlled URLs.

9.why: There are no HTML email templates that embed user input; delivery is a simulated in-browser message using textContent.

10.why: API errors are generic, but demo flows deliberately log and display mockToken and the MFA code in the page log and console.

11.why: Passwords are bcrypt-hashed in memory, yet MFA_CODE = "246810" is hardcoded in source and the client.

12.why: The fixed demo MFA secret 246810 acts as a default credential accepted by /api/verify-mfa.

13.why: Per-recovery attempt counters with BLOCK_MS plus IP clientRateAllowed limits throttle token, MFA, password, and recovery requests.

14.why: /api/recovery always returns the same generic success message and ignores whether the email is valid or registered (void validEmail).

15.why: Tokens come from crypto.getRandomValues 32-byte randomHex, are single-use and expiry-bound, and are bound to the requesting session’s recovery.
